title: returning a value whose type has a foreign `Promise` constituent is an escape of executable foreign provenance
notes:
poc/src/language/README.md, `VIBE1508`: 'executable foreign provenance escapes through an unsupported higher-order/return/store boundary.' This case carries NO `@throws` marker anywhere, which is its whole job: it is the control for a-trusted-union-with-a-promise-constituent-keeps-its-rejection-channel, and it localizes that case's extra VIBE1508 to the pre-existing union handling in `containsForeignExecutableValue` rather than to the trust rule. Two cases that diverge for one shared reason are worth more than one case that diverges for a reason nobody isolated.

2026-09-07 repair: native analysis now follows the lifted foreign success shape through await and aliases. Await on Result<string | Promise<string>, Panic> cannot consume its nested Promise, so both profiles retain VIBE1508 alongside VIBE1301. Native unit tests also execute the valid propagate-then-await form and refuse implicit coercion of the unconsumed payload. The original diagnostic list is unchanged; the historical file identity is retained.
